name: Vibe-coding leftovers
definition: Things left from building the app that a user should never see: template copy, demo data, debug UI, and copies of navigation or footer that drifted apart. Lorem ipsum, John/Jane Doe, example.com, TODO/FIXME on screen, 'Coming soon' sprawl and href="#" are already rule findings; do not repeat them.

checklist.question: Is template or scaffold copy left on screen ('Your tagline here', 'Feature 1', 'Card title', 'Welcome to your new app', 'Edit this page to get started')?

Are hard-coded numbers or records shown that look like demo data rather than the user's data (round marketing numbers like '10,000+ users' on a private dashboard, the same sample record repeated, 'Acme'-style placeholder companies)?
Is debug UI visible: JSON dumps, 'Debug' or 'Test' buttons, raw ids or state printed for the developer, a developer toolbar left on?

Do the header, navigation or footer differ from the reference screen's copy of them in a way that looks unintended (a link missing, a different label or order, an older logo text)? Answer none when this screen intentionally uses another layout (sign-in, landing page).

bad: The dashboard hero says 'Your tagline here'.
'Trusted by 50,000+ gardeners' on a signed-in page that lists the user's own three plants.
A 'Test toast' button next to 'Add plant'.
The footer on /notes links 'Help, Privacy'; on the reference /garden it links 'Help, Privacy, Terms' — copied before Terms was added.
good: An onboarding sample note 'Try editing me' that the app explains and lets the user delete.
The sign-in page has no main navigation: a deliberate layout.

severityRubric.high: debug UI or demo data that could mislead the user about their own data
severityRubric.medium: template copy or a drifted navigation on a core screen
severityRubric.low: a leftover on a rarely visited screen
